summary: Permission entropy causing inconsistent service-account access between prod-sandbox and staging
description: Issue summary: Intermittent 'access denied' failures observed for the llm-debugger service account when running diagnostic jobs in prod-sandbox; identical repro in staging shows different permission set. Impact: engineering-runbook diagnostics fail, delaying capacity investigations and failing automated oncall runbooks. Environment: prod-sandbox GCP project 'prod-sandbox-llm' and the staging project in us-east. Observed: some sessions assume the AWS role rl-llm-proxy and succeed, while others receiving identical tokens are denied; GCP service account impersonation appears to sometimes drop the iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission. Expected: consistent, reproducible IAM bindings for ephemeral debugging flows.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Observe token exchange logs in auth-proxy (auth-proxy logs show assumeRole request with session tags)
3) Repeat the command twice in short succession; one run may succeed and one fail with calls to iamservice:projects.serviceAccounts.iam.serviceAccounts.get: PERMISSION_DENIED
4) Confirm which principal (impersonator) is recorded in Cloud Audit Logs for the failed/successful attempts
logs:
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z auth-proxy INFO assume-role request start session_id=abc123 user=svc-ci
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z auth-proxy ERROR AssumeRoleDenied: sts:AssumeRole denied principal arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/rl-llm-proxy/session - policy evaluation: tag mismatch
projects/prod-sandbox-llm/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z: serviceAccount:llm-debugger@redwood-prod attempted iam.serviceAccounts.get => PERMISSION_DENIED
(See attached trace ids: trace:projects/trace/0123456789abcdef)
investigation_notes: Initial pattern: failures cluster around short bursts after a role tag-change push (0.1.3 -> 0.1.4) on 2026-03-09
Hypothesis A: session tag encoding truncation between GCP WIF and AWS STS is causing the AssumeRole condition to evaluate false
Hypothesis B: IAM binding propagation delay combined with ephemeral JIT roles leads to transient entropy in access matrices
Checked org-policy: no deny for iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on project, but tag-based condition exists on the AWS role that references attribute 'env' which sometimes is empty

Observed that the auth-proxy sometimes omits 'env' session tag when token length > 2048 bytes; seen in both staging and prod-sandbox but only produces access denied in prod-sandbox due to stricter role condition
comments: Priya Nair (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Filed after runbook failure during capacity validation. Attaching initial logs and trace ids.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed receipt. Will reproduce and capture Cloud Audit + AWS STS logs. Scheduling a short window with SRE to run controlled runs.

Maya Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced 2/5 failures in a 10-run batch. Correlated failures to token size > 2K and a non-UTF8 tag bit observed in the STS request. Pushed a debug build to auth-proxy to log full session tag payloads.
Tom Alvarez (Infra) - 2026-03-12: Noted a recent change in ops-scripts PR #78 that serializes tags differently (order changed). Rolling the PR back to test hypothesis B.

Liam O'Connor - 2026-03-13: After rollback, we ran 50 control executions; 0 failures. Next: add unit test ensuring tag order invariant and add validation in auth-proxy to reject >2048 byte combined headers. Planning follow-up ticket for long-term fix.
Priya Nair - 2026-03-13: Customer-facing impact minimal (internal tooling), but this blocks oncall diagnostics occasionally. Marking high priority for follow-up implementation.
temporary_workaround: Revert ops-scripts PR #78 which restored the previous deterministic tag serialization; avoid long session metadata payloads by forcing compact tag keys. SRE to run targeted replays for any missed diagnostics.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation deployed: rolled back serialization change and added a throttling guard in auth-proxy to reject overly long metadata. Long-term: add unit tests in ops-scripts and a validation layer at token-exchange to normalize tag order and truncate harmlessly while preserving required attributes. Creating follow-up INT ticket for automated regression tests and a small infra patch to normalize session tags across GCP->AWS flows.
followup_actions: INT-101235: Add auth-proxy unit tests for session tag ordering and size limits
INT-101236: Extend CI to run cross-cloud tag-encoding regression tests
